top_news.title: Government of Karnataka Announces Second Edition of Bengaluru Skill Summit
top_news.summary: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 7: The Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL), Government of Karnataka, today announced the second edition of the Bengaluru Skill Summit at a curtain raiser held at Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru. The summit will be held from 3 to 5 November 2026 at The Lalit Ashok Bengaluru, India. The curtain raiser was attended by Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Hon'ble Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood, Government of Karnataka; Sri Subodh Yadav, I.A.S., Principal Secretary to Government, Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship, Livelihood; Smt. Shivakantamma (Kanta) Naik, Chairperson, Karnataka Skill Development Corporation and Karnataka Vocational Training & Skill Development Corporation; Dr. E.V. Ramana Reddy, IAS (R), Chairman, Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA); Mr. Hiroshi Nawata, Consul General, Consulate General of Japan in Bengaluru; Dr. Ravi M. Tirlapur, K.A.S., Managing Director, Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC); Smt. Vasireddy Vijaya Jyothsna, I.A.S., Mission Director, National Livelihood Mission (NLM); and Smt. Shilpa M, I.A.S., Commissioner, Department of Industrial Training & Employment; and Rev. Fr. Dr. Victor Lobo SJ, Vice-Chancellor, St. Joseph's University. Under the patronage of Hon'ble Minister Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 is organised by the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL), Government of Karnataka, hosted by the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC), in collaboration with the Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA), with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) as Knowledge Partner. The Summit is managed by Trescon. Following a successful inaugural edition in November 2025 that drew over 6,500 footfall over three days, the 2026 summit returns as a strengthened, expanded and execution-focused platform. It is designed to move beyond dialogue into system-level workforce transformation, bringing together government, industry, academia and global partners to co-develop scalable skilling models. About the Theme The summit is anchored under the theme Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy, reflecting Karnataka's intent to build a workforce ecosystem that is scalable across sectors and geographies, structured through strong institutional systems, and driven by collaboration across stakeholders. Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 is expected to welcome: - 6,500+ Footfall - 150+ Speakers - 50+ Exhibitors - 100+ Partners - National and international delegations Four Thematic Tracks The summit builds on the inaugural edition with an execution lens focused on how scale is operationalised, systems are institutionalised, and synergy is translated into measurable outcomes. The programme is structured around four thematic tracks: Emerging Skills, Skills for All, Innovation and Global Skills. Emerging Skills: Preparing for green jobs, AI, Industry 4.0, the digital economy and other growth sectors. Skills for All: Advancing inclusion across women, youth, informal workers and the gig economy. Innovation: Showcasing global and local best practices and ecosystem innovations in skilling. Global Skills: Positioning Karnataka's workforce for global employability and mobility. Inauguration Day Inauguration of the 2nd edition of Bengaluru Skill Summit is scheduled for 3rd November at 5:00 PM by honorable Chief Minister of Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar in presence of Dr. G. Parameshwara, honorable Deputy Chief Minister and honorable Minister for Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood and Medical Education Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil and other dignitaries Plenary Stage The Plenary Stage will anchor the summit's leadership conversations, bringing together senior government leaders, industry experts, academia and workforce practitioners to examine the priorities shaping Workforce 2030. Discussions will explore future-ready skills, lifelong learning, inclusive workforce participation, global skills, AI-enabled transformation, employability and the role of policy and industry collaboration in building a future-ready workforce. Marquee Sessions The Plenary Stage will also feature a set of marquee sessions bringing high-level government leadership, state-level skilling perspectives and young skills champions into the centre of the Summit programme. Panel Discussion by Senior Ministers of the Government of Karnataka A high-level discussion on the topic Workforce 2030: Karnataka's Roadmap from Policy to Execution bringing together the following key portfolios to examine Karnataka's priorities for building a future-ready workforce and translating policy into measurable outcomes. - Large & Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development - Information Technology, Biotechnology (IT/BT) - Skill Development, Entrepreneurship, and Livelihood - Higher Education Panel Discussion by State Skill Development Secretaries A cross-state discussion on Learning from India's Leading Skills Ecosystems, bringing together Skill Development Secretaries to share practical approaches to strengthening skills systems, improving implementation and responding to evolving workforce needs. WorldSkills Champions Session A session featuring young winners from Karnataka who participated in WorldSkills 2026, Shanghai, sharing their experiences and journeys at the global skills competition. The session will spotlight how skills excellence can build confidence, open career pathways and create opportunities on the global stage. Leadership and Industry Participation The summit will feature 150+ speakers, bringing together senior government leaders, industry experts, academia, entrepreneurs and workforce practitioners from across India and international markets. Keynote Speakers will include Mr. Subroto Bagchi, Founder, Mindtree and Chairman, Vision Group for Skill Development, Government of Karnataka; Dr. Gururaj 'Desh' Deshpande, Entrepreneur, Philanthropist and Ecosystem Builder and Founder, Cascade Communications, Sycamore Networks, and Tejas Networks; and Dr. R. Balasubramaniayam, Member, NITI Aayog. Special Address Speakers will include Ms. Alina Alam, Founder and CEO, MITTI Cafe, and Air Commodore Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair (Kirti Chakra), Astronaut, Indian Space Research Organisation. Other key speakers on the Plenary Stage will include Mr. N.S. Parthasarathy, Managing Partner, Mela Ventures; Ms. Meena Ganesh, Co-founder & Chairperson, Portea Medical; Mrs. Uma Mahadevan, Development Commissioner, Government of Karnataka; Mr. Kaushik Mudda, Co-founder & CEO, Ethereal Machines; Mr. Rashmi Ranjan Mohapatra, CEO, World Skill Center and Odisha Skill Development Project II; Mekin Maheshwari, Founder & CEO, Udhyam Learning Foundation; Mr. Mohan Lakhamraju, Founder & CEO, Great Learning; Mr. Rajiv Kumar Sharma, Founder & Managing Director, Empower Pragati and Empower Foundation; Mr. Gopal Devanahalli, President, Skills Development Network; Dr. Nidhi Pundhir, SVP, Global CSR, HCL Tech & Director, HCL Foundation; and Mr. Vinay Kumar Swamy, Country Head, Pearson India. What's New in the 2026 Edition Precursor Events The 2026 edition introduced Precursor Events to build statewide momentum ahead of the Summit through thought leadership sessions hosted at Karnataka Digital Economy Mission's cluster events. Sessions were organised at the Mysuru Big Tech Show 2026 and HDB Techceleration 2026 in Hubballi, bringing the Workforce 2030 conversation to key technology and innovation ecosystems across Karnataka. Innovation Stage The summit architecture also expands with the Innovation Stage featuring applied skilling solutions, emerging models and pilots that address real workforce challenges. It will provide a platform for innovators, institutions and industry to showcase approaches that can be tested, adopted and scaled. Development Dialogue by Deshpande Skilling Hosted with the topic From Skilling to Employment: Getting Rural Youth into the Workforce will be a closed-door Development Dialogue hosted by Deshpande Foundation, focused on the transition from training to employment for rural youth. The dialogue will bring together government, skilling organisations, employers and development partners to examine how proven approaches can be strengthened, scaled and translated into sustainable employment pathways. Expo Arena The Expo Arena will provide a platform for organisations, institutions and innovators to showcase practical solutions, programmes and technologies shaping the future of skills and work. It will enable participants to discover proven models, emerging solutions and opportunities for collaboration. Kaushalya Karnataka Awards 2026 Following its introduction at the inaugural Bengaluru Skill Summit 2025, the Kaushalya Karnataka Awards returns for its second edition in 2026, continuing as an annual recognition of excellence in Karnataka's skilling and workforce development ecosystem. The awards will recognise organisations and institutions contributing to industry-led skilling, workforce transformation, industry-academia collaboration, inclusivity, innovation and measurable employment outcomes, alongside institutions and individuals driving excellence in skill development and training. The awards will be presented across Corporate Excellence and Institutional Excellence (Best Trainer, Best Trainee, Best Institution, Best Self-Help Group, and Best District) categories at the grand awards ceremony on 5 November 2026 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru. Skillathon 2026 As part of Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026, Skillathon invites individuals, teams, startups and organisations from across India to design how Karnataka can read its labour market and plan skilling around real demand. Participants will use publicly available government data to show what insights on jobs, skills and sectors can be drawn, how these can guide state policy, and how data from many sources can be brought together securely on a digital platform. The Value - Decode Demand: Map jobs, sectors and skill trends. - Validate Insights: Test assumptions and identify data gaps. - Guide Action: Inform skilling priorities and investments. - Shape Future Systems: Generate inputs for KSISU design. Parallel Roundtables Alongside the main summit programme, Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 will feature focused roundtables bringing together organisations and stakeholders across the skilling and workforce ecosystem. - Green Skills - organised by Recommerce and GIZ - Blue Collar Economy - organised by Seventh Sense - Smart Factories - organised by Automotive Skill Development Council - Academia 2030 - organised by Ripples Learning - CG + Trade Mission Roundtable - organised by Karnataka Skill Development Authority and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission - Vertical Transportation - organised by Bharath School of Vertical Transportation Training Pvt. Ltd. (BSVT) - Inclusive Skilling - organised by AssisTech Foundation (ATF) - Skills Development and International Mobility - organised by Indo-German Chamber of Commerce - From Knowledge to Capability: Integrating Employability into Education for Workforce 2030 - organised by National Skills Network - Healthcare & Life Sciences - organised by NextGen Health Minister's Quote Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Hon'ble Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood, Government of Karnataka, said, The inaugural edition in 2025 laid a strong foundation for collaboration and action. We now look forward to the second edition in November 2026, where stakeholders from across government, industry, academia, and the global community will come together to further strengthen partnerships and build a future-ready workforce. A Platform for Workforce Transformation Bengaluru Skill Summit is positioned as Karnataka's workforce systems platform, bringing together policymakers, industry leaders, employers, academia, training institutions, global partners and youth to strengthen the connection between education, skilling and employment. The summit provides a platform for policy dialogue, industry engagement, innovation, skills showcases and collaboration around scalable workforce solutions. The Summit's plenary and executive sessions are invitation-only and closed-door, while designated areas of the Expo, Innovation Stage and other public-facing activations are accessible to visitors. top_news.title: Kyptec Automation Expands USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable Portfolio for High Speed Industrial Imaging and Machine Vision Systems
top_news.summary: VMPL New Delhi [India], October 7: Kyptec Automation is strengthening its industrial imaging connectivity portfolio with the USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable developed for reliable communication between compatible industrial cameras and host computing systems used in machine vision, automated inspection and factory automation. The Kyptec Automation Machine Vision USB 3.0 A Male to Micro USB 3.0 Male With Screw Camera Cable combines a USB Type A connection for the host system with a Micro USB 3.0 connection incorporating locking screws for the camera side. The cable is available in standard lengths of 2 Meter, 3 Meter and 5 Meter, giving OEMs, machine builders and system integrators multiple options for different camera positions, industrial computer locations and machine geometries while remaining within one defined USB 3.0 machine vision connectivity platform. Modern machine vision systems depend on a complete imaging architecture in which the camera, lens, illumination, acquisition interface, cable, host controller, processing hardware and machine vision software must operate together. As industrial cameras capture increasingly detailed image information at higher acquisition rates, reliable communication between the camera and processing system becomes an important part of overall inspection stability. The USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable is therefore not simply a connection between two devices. It forms part of the image acquisition path through which industrial camera data must be transferred consistently to the host system for processing, measurement, identification and automated inspection. USB 3.0 connectivity is particularly relevant for compatible industrial imaging systems where high speed camera data needs to be transferred to an industrial computer or processing platform within the designed machine architecture. Selecting a USB 3.0 camera cable should therefore begin with the actual imaging requirement rather than connector compatibility alone. Camera resolution, frame rate, pixel format, acquisition frequency, cable length, host controller architecture, connector retention, routing conditions, machine movement and production duty cycle should all be considered before the final cable configuration is approved. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable uses a USB Type A male connector on the host side and a Micro USB 3.0 male connector with locking screws on the camera side. This camera side locking arrangement is particularly relevant to industrial imaging installations where the connection may need to remain secure throughout prolonged production operation. Industrial cameras can be installed inside inspection machines, beside conveyors, within automated assembly systems, above production lines or inside purpose built imaging stations. In these applications, cable security and controlled routing can become important elements of reliable camera integration. An industrial camera cable should also be evaluated according to its operating environment. Machine vision equipment can expose cable assemblies to repeated handling, movement, equipment vibration, constrained routing paths and continuous production operation. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable uses highly flexible PVC cable construction intended for industrial imaging applications. The cable architecture is designed for applications including machine vision systems, industrial cameras, scientific imaging, automated inspection, product testing, image recognition, data acquisition and factory automation. The relationship between camera bandwidth and cable architecture is another important consideration. A machine vision camera generates image data according to sensor resolution, frame rate, pixel format and acquisition settings. Increasing any of these parameters can increase the volume of data that must move through the complete imaging system. Engineers should therefore evaluate the USB 3.0 machine vision cable together with the camera and host architecture instead of assuming that interface designation alone guarantees the required system performance. The host controller, processing platform, acquisition software and storage architecture can all influence how successfully the complete system manages the required image stream. This becomes even more important where several industrial cameras are integrated into one inspection machine. Multiple cameras can create a significantly different system load compared with a single camera architecture. Engineers may need to consider how camera traffic is distributed across host controller resources, how images are processed, whether acquisition occurs simultaneously and what operating margin is required for continuous production. The cable remains one component within this complete data path, which is why machine vision connectivity should be qualified under the actual camera and host configuration that will be used in the production machine. Industrial camera connectivity should be engineered as part of the complete machine vision system rather than treated as an ordinary computer accessory, said Nitin Aggarwal, Co Founder and CEO of Kyptec Automation. When OEMs and system integrators design a USB 3.0 camera architecture, they need to consider camera data requirements, cable length, locking mechanism, routing, host controller capability and production conditions together. Our objective is to provide a structured USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable platform that supports reliable industrial camera integration across machine vision, automated inspection and factory automation systems. Connector retention is particularly important in industrial machinery because camera communication needs to remain stable during normal equipment operation. A locking USB 3.0 camera cable can provide additional mechanical retention at the industrial camera connection compared with a connector that relies only on insertion force. The locking screws incorporated into the Micro USB 3.0 camera side connection are intended to support secure installation with compatible industrial cameras. Correct installation should nevertheless include appropriate cable routing, strain management, connector clearance and suitable bend conditions so that mechanical forces are not unnecessarily transferred to the camera connector. Cable length should also be selected according to system geometry rather than simply choosing the longest available option. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable is available in standard 2 Meter, 3 Meter and 5 Meter lengths. Machine builders should evaluate the actual distance between camera and host system, cable tray routing, cabinet position, service accessibility and any movement within the machine before standardizing the required cable length. A correctly planned installation can reduce unnecessary cable loops, excessive tension and difficult routing while making machine commissioning and future maintenance more structured. The selection of a USB camera cable for machine vision also depends on how the camera is physically integrated into the equipment. A camera mounted close to an industrial computer can have very different routing requirements from a camera positioned remotely inside a large inspection machine. Similarly, a fixed camera installation can create different mechanical requirements from an application where part of the cable route is exposed to repeated movement. Defining these conditions early in the machine design process allows the connectivity architecture to be treated as an engineered subsystem rather than as a component selected after the camera installation has already been completed. For OEMs manufacturing multiple machines, standardization of the USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable can support repeatable engineering and production. Once camera type, host architecture, cable length and installation method have been qualified, manufacturers can define approved configurations for individual machine platforms. These configurations can become part of engineering drawings, bills of material, assembly documentation, commissioning procedures and replacement planning. A structured approach can also help system integrators maintain greater consistency when the same imaging architecture is deployed across multiple production lines or customer installations. Automated visual inspection is one of the environments where reliable camera connectivity becomes particularly important. Machine vision cameras may be used to inspect product dimensions, surface condition, component presence, assembly position, labels, printed information, packaging quality or other manufacturing characteristics. Images captured by the camera must reach the processing system so that software can analyse the inspection area and provide the required output within the machine cycle. Stable connectivity therefore contributes to the continuity of the complete acquisition and processing architecture. Industrial imaging installations also need to consider electrical and mechanical conditions surrounding the cable route. Industrial computers, motors, automation equipment, power cables, moving assemblies and control systems can all exist within the same machine environment. Engineers should plan the camera cable path carefully and maintain appropriate separation, routing discipline and mechanical protection according to the design of the equipment. Cable qualification should be performed with the actual industrial camera, host computer, acquisition settings and machine operating conditions rather than relying only on individual component specifications. The machine vision camera cable therefore needs to be understood as part of the wider industrial imaging system. Camera connectivity influences how the imaging hardware is installed, how reliably the camera communicates with the host and how easily the machine can be manufactured, commissioned and serviced. By developing a dedicated USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable platform, Kyptec Automation is focusing specifically on connectivity requirements associated with industrial cameras, machine vision systems and automated inspection rather than positioning the product as general purpose USB connectivity. The USB 3.0 machine vision cable category also supports the broader requirement for clearly defined machine vision components within OEM equipment. Engineering teams increasingly standardize cameras, optics, lighting, cables, computers and other components so that each machine configuration can be reproduced consistently. A defined industrial camera cable architecture allows cable length, connection type, locking method and routing requirement to become part of this standardization process. This can be particularly valuable in machines intended for continuous production where component consistency and serviceability are important considerations throughout the operational life of the equipment. Machine vision adoption continues to expand across electronics production, packaging, pharmaceutical inspection, automotive manufacturing, component measurement, product identification, assembly verification, surface inspection and many other factory automation environments. Although these applications can require different cameras, lenses, lighting arrangements and image processing methods, all of them depend on a reliable connection between the camera and processing system. USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable selection therefore represents an important engineering decision for applications using compatible USB industrial cameras. Kyptec Automation is strengthening its specialist machine vision connectivity portfolio around this system level requirement. The combination of USB 3.0 connectivity, USB Type A host interface, Micro USB 3.0 camera connection with locking screws, flexible cable construction and multiple standard length options provides OEMs and system integrators with a defined platform for compatible industrial imaging systems. The objective is to support camera connectivity across automated inspection, machine vision, scientific imaging, product testing, image recognition and factory automation applications while maintaining a clear relationship between camera requirements, cable architecture and host system design. By expanding its focus on USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable technology, Kyptec Automation is strengthening its position within industrial camera connectivity and machine vision system integration. The product platform addresses the practical relationship between high speed image acquisition, camera connection security, cable length planning, host architecture, machine layout and long term industrial operation. For OEMs, machine builders and system integrators developing modern automated inspection equipment, this complete system perspective provides a structured foundation for selecting and standardizing camera connectivity within machine vision applications. top_news.title: 10 Rising Personalities Making a Mark Across Industries
top_news.summary: VMPL New Delhi [India], October 7: India's rapidly evolving business and professional landscape is being shaped by a new generation of ambitious individuals creating meaningful impact across diverse industries. From healthcare and technology to wellness, energy, media and entrepreneurship, these 10 rising personalities are driving innovation, building impactful ventures and contributing to India's growth story. Their vision, determination and industry expertise reflect the changing face of leadership and highlight the inspiring journeys of individuals who are making a mark across sectors. 1. Sustainability Communicator of the Year 2026: Sunil Sushila Sharma Champions Rural India Veteran journalist, rural communication strategist and media entrepreneur Sunil Sushila Sharma has been recognised as Sustainability Communicator / Influencer of the Year 2026 at the BW Sustainability Awards 2026. His work focuses on agriculture, farmers, rural development and environmental sustainability. Sharma's journalism highlights five interconnected pillars of rural India: Forests, Soil, Water, Mountains, and Farmers . Through television, digital media and grassroots storytelling, he has worked to bring greater attention to farmers, natural farming, water conservation, soil health and rural entrepreneurship. He is also the founder of Farmfare TV, envisioned as a 24x7 agritainment OTT platform dedicated to farming, rural India and agri-business. His initiatives include Mitti Ke Mahanayak, Jangal Mitti Jal Pahad, Ram Ram Sa and Jai Jai Kisan. With more than 500 agriculture and rural-focused programmes, Sharma continues to promote solution-driven journalism and create a stronger national conversation around sustainable agriculture and rural transformation. 2. Shubham Sharma: Driving India's Hydrogen and Clean-Energy Innovation Shubham Sharma, Co-Founder and CEO of Hydrotech Clean Energy Pvt Ltd, is contributing to India's growing hydrogen and clean-energy sector through innovative HHO-based technologies. Since 2013, he has led the development of solutions focused on engine Decarbonising , fuel efficiency, emission reduction, and sustainable operations. Hydrotech Clean Energy Pvt Ltd specializes in engine decarbonization machines, hydrogen fuel-saving systems for diesel generators, and on-demand HHO solutions for automotive and industrial applications. The company is also witnessing growing demand for its HHO solutions for boilers and furnaces, reflecting the expanding adoption of hydrogen-based technologies across industrial applications. With a network of more than 2,000 decarbonization centers across India and exports to over 18 countries, Hydrotech has established a growing international presence. Recognized among the Forbes India DGEMS Select 200 Companies of 2025, Hydrotech continues to strengthen its clean-tech portfolio. With three granted patents and two pending applications, the company is advancing hydrogen technology and positioning itself as a Best manufacturer of Engine Decarbon machine in the evolving clean-energy industry. 3. Dt. Kajal Aggarwal: Transforming Weight Loss Through Sustainable Nutrition & Women's Wellness Dt. Kajal Aggarwal is a renowned Indian dietitian, nutritionist, and wellness entrepreneur known for her expertise in sustainable weight management and women's health. Through her nutrition practice, she and her team have helped 30,000+ clients across 28 countries achieve healthier and more sustainable lifestyle goals. With a growing digital community of 314K+ Instagram followers and an additional 85K+ followers focused on fertility and women's health, Kajal has established a strong presence in India's nutrition and wellness industry. Her approach focuses on personalised nutrition, Indian home-cooked food, lifestyle changes, and understanding factors such as eating habits, sleep, stress, gut health, and hormonal concerns. Her areas of expertise include weight loss, PCOS nutrition, thyroid nutrition, gut health, women's wellness, and fertility nutrition. Through consultations, educational content, and digital platforms, Dt. Kajal Aggarwal continues to make practical, evidence-informed nutrition more accessible worldwide. 4. Meenal Malhotra Is Making Room for Childhood in Indian Fashion Why should kids grow up? is the question behind Meenal Malhotra's Anaario. The Indian children's wear brand takes the energy of childhood seriously, making clothes that are expressive enough for children to enjoy and considered enough for parents to choose with confidence. The collection spans newborns to 16 year olds, with everyday clothing, festive pieces, a bamboo baby range and bamboo innerwear. Fabric choices follow the garment: organic cotton features across the range, while selected occasion wear uses organic handloom cotton. Colour, print and comfort are central to the design, without asking children to dress like miniature adults. Anaario makes each piece after it is ordered. Families can request adjustments to size, length, colour, fabric and design, including matching outfits for siblings and parents. Made to order production gives those choices a practical place in the process: the garment is made for the child who will wear it. Malhotra's idea is straightforward: childhood has its own character, and children's clothing should make space for it. Anaario turns that idea into a wardrobe that feels playful, personal and easy to wear. 5. Sangeet Sejpal: Connecting Indian Industry with Global Business Opportunities Sangeet Sejpal, Director of Shezle Imperio Private Limited, is an emerging Indian business leader focused on building strategic connections across the chemical and industrial ecosystem. Through Shezle Imperio, Sejpal works with manufacturers, industrial enterprises and commercial partners across chemicals, petrochemicals, specialty materials, oils and fats, and industrial by-products. His approach centers on connecting capabilities, resources and markets to create long-term and mutually valuable business opportunities. With an international outlook spanning India, Mauritius, Africa and emerging global markets, Sejpal focuses on developing cross-border relationships, facilitating market opportunities and strengthening commercial partnerships. His vision extends beyond conventional trade building a globally connected business platform that brings together industry expertise, international markets and strategic partnerships. Combining entrepreneurial thinking, sector knowledge and global ambition, Sangeet Sejpal represents a new generation of Indian business leaders creating meaningful connections across industries and borders. 6. Anand Rathore: Shaping the Future of AI Ways of Working As artificial intelligence rapidly transforms businesses, governments, and society, Anand Rathore is emerging as a voice focused on a question beyond AI adoption: How should humans and organisations work with AI responsibly? Anand is the pioneer of AIWoW - AI Ways of Working and the President of the Artificial Intelligence Ways of Working Council (AIWoW Council), an initiative focused on building practical approaches for responsible, human-centric and sustainable AI adoption. His work aims to bridge the gap between AI capability and organisational responsibility by addressing governance, human accountability, ethics, sustainability and the evolving relationship between humans and intelligent systems. A program management leader with 18+ years of experience in digital transformation and enterprise delivery, Anand combines finance, business, technology, and legal perspectives. His academic background includes an MBA in Finance, PGDBF, LLB in Corporate Law and B.Com, complemented by professional credentials including PMP, PRINCE2 Agile, Scrum Master, and DevOps Practitioner. He is the author of the 456-page book AIWoW - AI Ways of Working and has published research on Empathic Intelligence and the AI Lifecycle Loop. Through the AIWoW Council, Rathore is bringing together leaders, researchers, academics, and professionals to shape practical standards, certification, research, and responsible AI leadership positioning how we work with AI as an equally important conversation as what AI can do. Explore www.aiwowcouncil.org. 7.Dr. Aarti: The Visionary Minds Behind ADNA Naturals and India's Herbal Baby Care Revolution At a time when many choose to slow down, Dr. Aarti chose to innovate for the next generation alongside her daughter, Dr. Namrata. Holding a PhD from NLSIU Bangalore and having completed post-doctoral research at Stetson University, Florida, Dr. Aarti dedicated years to child welfare, even authoring the acclaimed book Protection of Children from Internet Harms: A Global Concern (Cyberbullying). Today, Dr. Aarti's lifelong commitment to child safety has transitioned into the physical world of clean infant skincare, co-founding ADNA Naturals with Dr. Namrata based on a strict brand ethos: Traditionally Trusted, Scientifically Tested. The idea for ADNA Naturals sparked when Dr. Aarti's grandson suffered a minor fall. Dr. Aarti prepared a traditional kitchen paste of herbs used by grandmothers for generations. But one haunting thought stayed with her: what happens when NaniMaa is not around? Dr. Aarti quickly realized that modern, busy parents-like Dr. Namrata, who balanced a demanding career as an elite researcher with winning Mrs. India 2021-simply do not have the time to forage and grind fresh herbs from scratch. Finding a total lack of clean, ready-made natural alternatives on retail shelves, Dr. Aarti and Dr. Namrata set out together to bridge this market gap. Our traditional knowledge embodies a wealth of wisdom used over millennia. We wanted to preserve these customary practices in a way that fits seamlessly into the bustling schedule of today's parents, notes the founding team. This became the ultimate inspiration behind ADNA Naturals-bringing NaniMaa wisdom into convenient, contemporary baby care by combining traditional ingredients with modern product development and strict safety considerations. Together, Dr. Aarti and Dr. Namrata turned generations of care, deep research, and intuitive motherhood into a true legacy. Proudly known as a NaniMaa & Mom Brand, ADNA Naturals is uniquely co-founded by this powerhouse mother-daughter duo of academic researchers. While building the brand's foundation, Dr. Namrata leveraged her extensive global travels to interview mothers and study baby skin and hair formulations worldwide. This deep research by Dr. Namrata, combined with Dr. Aarti's generational wisdom, directly led to their flagship breakthrough: the Herbal Baby Balm for Hurts & Falls. Together, Dr. Aarti and Dr. Namrata perfectly blend traditional Indian heritage with contemporary scientific safety standards. While Dr. Aarti's journey delivers a powerful message that age does not limit ambition, the leadership of Dr. Namrata ensures the brand remains deeply relevant for today's generation. By combining life experience, global research, and a shared passion for child safety, Dr. Aarti and Dr. Namrata have successfully transformed a grandmother's love into a trusted, modern baby-care revolution. 8. Dr. Omkar Prasad Baidya: Advancing Universal Ethics and World Peace Dr. Omkar Prasad Baidya is a distinguished Indian physician, philosopher, and peace advocate known for his work on universal ethics, morality, and world peace. Originally from Tripura, he completed his MBBS and MD from the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), Imphal, and later pursued advanced research at King George's Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, under an ICMR Fellowship. Dr. Baidya's philosophy explores morality as a biological and evolutionary trait, emphasizing values such as compassion, cooperation, and non-violence. He believes that ethical education can help develop a more peaceful and responsible global society. He has authored books including A Path to World Peace, Morality Beyond Human Brain, and Universal Ethics and World Peace. His contributions to ethics and humanity have also received various recognitions, including the Mahatma Gandhi Nobel Peace Award and Asia Peace Prize. 9. Krish 'KungFuKrish': 16-Year-Old Founder Launches 100,000-Km Virtual Walkathon for Global Peace Krish, popularly known as KungFuKrish, has launched a 100,000-Km Virtual Walkathon for Global Peace through the Walk With Me Movement. At just 16, the young founder and CEO is taking the concept of city-based walkathons to a global audience by inviting people to walk from wherever they are and contribute their kilometres toward one collective goal. The initiative aims to bring together 10,000 participants and achieve a combined walking distance of 100,000 kilometres. According to figures provided by the organisers, the campaign has already received nearly 1,000 registrations and accumulated around 2,000 kilometres. Participants can walk in their neighbourhoods, schools, workplaces, parks or other suitable locations and submit their walking distance as part of the campaign. The initiative follows two physical walkathons organised by Krish and the Walk With Me Movement in major Indian metropolitan cities. The virtual format allows participation beyond geographical boundaries. Built around the message Every Step Counts, the campaign presents walking as a simple, accessible way for people to participate in a collective symbolic movement for global peace. 10. Ravi Arya: The Beverage Industry Leader Elevating Coffee, Hospitality & Customer Experience Ravi Arya is a hospitality and beverage industry professional with over 15 years of experience spanning workplace beverages, speciality coffee, tea, retail operations, and F&B. Previously, at Dunkin', Ravi was part of the expansion team that opened 18 restaurants in two years, earning the Dunkin Service Excellence Award. With his extensive experience across hospitality, coffee, beverages, retail operations, and customer experience, Ravi Arya continues to contribute to the evolution of the beverage industry through innovation, sustainability, quality, and operational excellence. top_news.summary: PRNewswire Chandigarh [India], October 7: Top-ranked global universities from 13 countries including US, UK, Australia, New Zealand and France offered study abroad opportunities to Chandigarh University (CU) students through student exchange programs, semester transfer programs, international transfer programs, credit transfer programs, winter school, summer school, internships, research internships and short-term programs with scholarship during the two-day 'International Education Expo 2026' at CU Campus. The inauguration ceremony of 'International Education Expo 2026' was graced by dignitaries including Prof (Dr) Nelson Ribeiro, Vice-Rector of the Catholic University of Portugal, Prof (Dr) Todor Radev, President of Varna University of Management, Bulgaria, Prof (Dr) Matilde Maria Olarte Martinez, Vice-Rector for Culture, Heritage, Sustainable Development, and Campus Development at the University of Salamanca, Spain, Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal, Vice-Chancellor, Chandigarh University and Prof (Dr) Rajan Sharma, Executive Director, International Affairs, Chandigarh University along with senior representatives from 29 universities including heads of international affairs, deans, directors, recruitment officers and other academic delegates. Organised by Chandigarh University, the 'International Education Expo 2026' provided CU students access to world-class study abroad opportunities at top-ranked global universities with scholarship. This Expo was attended by delegates from leading global universities from 13 countries Including UK, USA, France, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Portugal, Brazil, Malaysia, UAE, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and Ethiopia who offered study abroad opportunities through 18 International Transfer Programs, six Student Exchange Programs, three Short Term Programs, Summer School and Research Internships with scholarships. A total of 9,900 students participated in the two-day event which provided Chandigarh University students with information regarding overseas education and guidance for admission process to world-class programs for global employment opportunities. As a part of the Chandigarh University's international collaboration to provide global education opportunities for its students through academic partnerships with the top educational institutions in fields like AI, engineering, business, and research, the 'International Education Expo 2026' was attended by top-ranked universities including Johns Hopkins University (USA), University of Newcastle (Australia), Wayne State University (USA), Massey University (New Zealand), Western Sydney University (Australia), University of Southampton (UK), University of Wollongong (Australia), Deakin University (Australia), University of Huddersfield, United Kingdom, University of Plymouth, United Kingdom and Pittsburg State University, USA. In all, the 'International Education Expo 2026' - an initiative aimed at offering Chandigarh University students excellent opportunities for education and employment in countries across the world - was attended by six universities from the UK, 8 universities from US, 4 universities from Australia, 2 universities each from France, Ethiopia and North Macedonia, one university each from Brazil, New Zealand, Malaysia, UAE, and Bulgaria participated to offer study abroad opportunities to Chandigarh University students across streams including Engineering, Management through student exchange programs, international transfer programs, credit transfer programs, winter school, summer school, research internships and short-term programs. A total of 9,900 students participated in the two-day 'International Education Expo 2026' to explore global opportunities at top universities across the world for their future education and careers. Besides serving as a significant platform to further strengthen academic partnerships and collaboration between universities from various countries and Chandigarh University, 'International Education Expo 2026' provided Chandigarh University students an opportunity to connect directly with world-class universities, understand study-abroad opportunities and choose the right path for their future education and careers. Speaking at the inauguration of 'International Education Expo 2026', Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal, Vice-Chancellor, Chandigarh University said, As a result of the internationalisation of education, the world has transformed into a global village and global education has become a necessity for students to get equipped with 21st-century competencies, cross-cultural empathy and adaptable skill sets required to navigate and thrive in this highly integrated landscape. So besides providing world-class education at CU campus, Chandigarh University not only provides information regarding overseas education, student exchange, and transfer programs but also offers guidance on international academic environments, global career prospects and making the right educational choices for the future. In this context, the International Education Expo 2026 is a significant platform for Chandigarh University students to connect directly with top universities worldwide and gain insights into higher education opportunities abroad. At the same time, platforms like the Education Expo play a pivotal role in strengthening academic collaborations, student mobility, joint research, and knowledge exchange between top universities from various countries,. In today's globalized era, international education serves as a crucial medium for equipping students with the knowledge, skills, and broad perspectives needed to compete on a global stage. Chandigarh University is committed to providing global exposure alongside top-tier education to as many students as possible. To offer students global academic and research experiences, Chandigarh University has established over 540 international partnerships with renowned universities worldwide. As a result of these collaborations, more than 2300 CU students have got the opportunity to study at prestigious global universities in United States of America, Australia, Canada and UK among other European countries and other nations all across the world through semester exchange, international programs and internships. As of the Chandigarh University's international collaboration to offer world-class education, CU has more than 2100 visiting international faculty members including 560 international research network scholars and more than 3,000 international students from 65 countries study at Chandigarh University. Thus, going beyond mere education, Chandigarh University prepares students for global competition, enabling them to understand diverse cultures, engage in academic collaborations, explore new research avenues, exchange ideas with peers from different backgrounds, and unlock doors to future career pathways. About Chandigarh University Chandigarh University is a NAAC A+ Grade University and QS World Ranked University. This autonomous educational institution is approved by UGC and is located near Chandigarh in the state of Punjab. It is the youngest university in India and the only private university in Punjab to be honoured with A+ Grade by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council). CU offers more than 109 UG and PG programs in the field of engineering, management, pharmacy, law, architecture, journalism, animation, hotel management, commerce, and others. articles.title: Government of Karnataka Announces Second Edition of Bengaluru Skill Summit
articles.summary: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 7: The Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL), Government of Karnataka, today announced the second edition of the Bengaluru Skill Summit at a curtain raiser held at Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru. The summit will be held from 3 to 5 November 2026 at The Lalit Ashok Bengaluru, India. The curtain raiser was attended by Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Hon'ble Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood, Government of Karnataka; Sri Subodh Yadav, I.A.S., Principal Secretary to Government, Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship, Livelihood; Smt. Shivakantamma (Kanta) Naik, Chairperson, Karnataka Skill Development Corporation and Karnataka Vocational Training & Skill Development Corporation; Dr. E.V. Ramana Reddy, IAS (R), Chairman, Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA); Mr. Hiroshi Nawata, Consul General, Consulate General of Japan in Bengaluru; Dr. Ravi M. Tirlapur, K.A.S., Managing Director, Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC); Smt. Vasireddy Vijaya Jyothsna, I.A.S., Mission Director, National Livelihood Mission (NLM); and Smt. Shilpa M, I.A.S., Commissioner, Department of Industrial Training & Employment; and Rev. Fr. Dr. Victor Lobo SJ, Vice-Chancellor, St. Joseph's University. Under the patronage of Hon'ble Minister Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 is organised by the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL), Government of Karnataka, hosted by the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC), in collaboration with the Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA), with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) as Knowledge Partner. The Summit is managed by Trescon. Following a successful inaugural edition in November 2025 that drew over 6,500 footfall over three days, the 2026 summit returns as a strengthened, expanded and execution-focused platform. It is designed to move beyond dialogue into system-level workforce transformation, bringing together government, industry, academia and global partners to co-develop scalable skilling models. About the Theme The summit is anchored under the theme Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy, reflecting Karnataka's intent to build a workforce ecosystem that is scalable across sectors and geographies, structured through strong institutional systems, and driven by collaboration across stakeholders. Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 is expected to welcome: - 6,500+ Footfall - 150+ Speakers - 50+ Exhibitors - 100+ Partners - National and international delegations Four Thematic Tracks The summit builds on the inaugural edition with an execution lens focused on how scale is operationalised, systems are institutionalised, and synergy is translated into measurable outcomes. The programme is structured around four thematic tracks: Emerging Skills, Skills for All, Innovation and Global Skills. Emerging Skills: Preparing for green jobs, AI, Industry 4.0, the digital economy and other growth sectors. Skills for All: Advancing inclusion across women, youth, informal workers and the gig economy. Innovation: Showcasing global and local best practices and ecosystem innovations in skilling. Global Skills: Positioning Karnataka's workforce for global employability and mobility. Inauguration Day Inauguration of the 2nd edition of Bengaluru Skill Summit is scheduled for 3rd November at 5:00 PM by honorable Chief Minister of Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar in presence of Dr. G. Parameshwara, honorable Deputy Chief Minister and honorable Minister for Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood and Medical Education Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil and other dignitaries Plenary Stage The Plenary Stage will anchor the summit's leadership conversations, bringing together senior government leaders, industry experts, academia and workforce practitioners to examine the priorities shaping Workforce 2030. Discussions will explore future-ready skills, lifelong learning, inclusive workforce participation, global skills, AI-enabled transformation, employability and the role of policy and industry collaboration in building a future-ready workforce. Marquee Sessions The Plenary Stage will also feature a set of marquee sessions bringing high-level government leadership, state-level skilling perspectives and young skills champions into the centre of the Summit programme. Panel Discussion by Senior Ministers of the Government of Karnataka A high-level discussion on the topic Workforce 2030: Karnataka's Roadmap from Policy to Execution bringing together the following key portfolios to examine Karnataka's priorities for building a future-ready workforce and translating policy into measurable outcomes. - Large & Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development - Information Technology, Biotechnology (IT/BT) - Skill Development, Entrepreneurship, and Livelihood - Higher Education Panel Discussion by State Skill Development Secretaries A cross-state discussion on Learning from India's Leading Skills Ecosystems, bringing together Skill Development Secretaries to share practical approaches to strengthening skills systems, improving implementation and responding to evolving workforce needs. WorldSkills Champions Session A session featuring young winners from Karnataka who participated in WorldSkills 2026, Shanghai, sharing their experiences and journeys at the global skills competition. The session will spotlight how skills excellence can build confidence, open career pathways and create opportunities on the global stage. Leadership and Industry Participation The summit will feature 150+ speakers, bringing together senior government leaders, industry experts, academia, entrepreneurs and workforce practitioners from across India and international markets. Keynote Speakers will include Mr. Subroto Bagchi, Founder, Mindtree and Chairman, Vision Group for Skill Development, Government of Karnataka; Dr. Gururaj 'Desh' Deshpande, Entrepreneur, Philanthropist and Ecosystem Builder and Founder, Cascade Communications, Sycamore Networks, and Tejas Networks; and Dr. R. Balasubramaniayam, Member, NITI Aayog. Special Address Speakers will include Ms. Alina Alam, Founder and CEO, MITTI Cafe, and Air Commodore Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair (Kirti Chakra), Astronaut, Indian Space Research Organisation. Other key speakers on the Plenary Stage will include Mr. N.S. Parthasarathy, Managing Partner, Mela Ventures; Ms. Meena Ganesh, Co-founder & Chairperson, Portea Medical; Mrs. Uma Mahadevan, Development Commissioner, Government of Karnataka; Mr. Kaushik Mudda, Co-founder & CEO, Ethereal Machines; Mr. Rashmi Ranjan Mohapatra, CEO, World Skill Center and Odisha Skill Development Project II; Mekin Maheshwari, Founder & CEO, Udhyam Learning Foundation; Mr. Mohan Lakhamraju, Founder & CEO, Great Learning; Mr. Rajiv Kumar Sharma, Founder & Managing Director, Empower Pragati and Empower Foundation; Mr. Gopal Devanahalli, President, Skills Development Network; Dr. Nidhi Pundhir, SVP, Global CSR, HCL Tech & Director, HCL Foundation; and Mr. Vinay Kumar Swamy, Country Head, Pearson India. What's New in the 2026 Edition Precursor Events The 2026 edition introduced Precursor Events to build statewide momentum ahead of the Summit through thought leadership sessions hosted at Karnataka Digital Economy Mission's cluster events. Sessions were organised at the Mysuru Big Tech Show 2026 and HDB Techceleration 2026 in Hubballi, bringing the Workforce 2030 conversation to key technology and innovation ecosystems across Karnataka. Innovation Stage The summit architecture also expands with the Innovation Stage featuring applied skilling solutions, emerging models and pilots that address real workforce challenges. It will provide a platform for innovators, institutions and industry to showcase approaches that can be tested, adopted and scaled. Development Dialogue by Deshpande Skilling Hosted with the topic From Skilling to Employment: Getting Rural Youth into the Workforce will be a closed-door Development Dialogue hosted by Deshpande Foundation, focused on the transition from training to employment for rural youth. The dialogue will bring together government, skilling organisations, employers and development partners to examine how proven approaches can be strengthened, scaled and translated into sustainable employment pathways. Expo Arena The Expo Arena will provide a platform for organisations, institutions and innovators to showcase practical solutions, programmes and technologies shaping the future of skills and work. It will enable participants to discover proven models, emerging solutions and opportunities for collaboration. Kaushalya Karnataka Awards 2026 Following its introduction at the inaugural Bengaluru Skill Summit 2025, the Kaushalya Karnataka Awards returns for its second edition in 2026, continuing as an annual recognition of excellence in Karnataka's skilling and workforce development ecosystem. The awards will recognise organisations and institutions contributing to industry-led skilling, workforce transformation, industry-academia collaboration, inclusivity, innovation and measurable employment outcomes, alongside institutions and individuals driving excellence in skill development and training. The awards will be presented across Corporate Excellence and Institutional Excellence (Best Trainer, Best Trainee, Best Institution, Best Self-Help Group, and Best District) categories at the grand awards ceremony on 5 November 2026 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru. Skillathon 2026 As part of Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026, Skillathon invites individuals, teams, startups and organisations from across India to design how Karnataka can read its labour market and plan skilling around real demand. Participants will use publicly available government data to show what insights on jobs, skills and sectors can be drawn, how these can guide state policy, and how data from many sources can be brought together securely on a digital platform. The Value - Decode Demand: Map jobs, sectors and skill trends. - Validate Insights: Test assumptions and identify data gaps. - Guide Action: Inform skilling priorities and investments. - Shape Future Systems: Generate inputs for KSISU design. Parallel Roundtables Alongside the main summit programme, Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 will feature focused roundtables bringing together organisations and stakeholders across the skilling and workforce ecosystem. - Green Skills - organised by Recommerce and GIZ - Blue Collar Economy - organised by Seventh Sense - Smart Factories - organised by Automotive Skill Development Council - Academia 2030 - organised by Ripples Learning - CG + Trade Mission Roundtable - organised by Karnataka Skill Development Authority and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission - Vertical Transportation - organised by Bharath School of Vertical Transportation Training Pvt. Ltd. (BSVT) - Inclusive Skilling - organised by AssisTech Foundation (ATF) - Skills Development and International Mobility - organised by Indo-German Chamber of Commerce - From Knowledge to Capability: Integrating Employability into Education for Workforce 2030 - organised by National Skills Network - Healthcare & Life Sciences - organised by NextGen Health Minister's Quote Dr. Sharanprakash Rudrappa Patil, Hon'ble Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship & Livelihood, Government of Karnataka, said, The inaugural edition in 2025 laid a strong foundation for collaboration and action. We now look forward to the second edition in November 2026, where stakeholders from across government, industry, academia, and the global community will come together to further strengthen partnerships and build a future-ready workforce. A Platform for Workforce Transformation Bengaluru Skill Summit is positioned as Karnataka's workforce systems platform, bringing together policymakers, industry leaders, employers, academia, training institutions, global partners and youth to strengthen the connection between education, skilling and employment. The summit provides a platform for policy dialogue, industry engagement, innovation, skills showcases and collaboration around scalable workforce solutions. The Summit's plenary and executive sessions are invitation-only and closed-door, while designated areas of the Expo, Innovation Stage and other public-facing activations are accessible to visitors. Event Details Event name: Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026 Theme: Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy Dates: 3 to 5 November 2026 Venue: The Lalit Ashok Bengaluru, India Organised by: Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL), Government of Karnataka Hosted by: Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC) In collaboration with: Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA) Knowledge Partner: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) Managed by: Trescon About Bengaluru Skill Summit Bengaluru Skill Summit is Karnataka's workforce systems platform, positioned to strengthen the state's leadership in workforce development, bridge gaps between education, skilling and employment, and build scalable skilling systems aligned with emerging sectors. The Summit is positioned as a long-term annual platform contributing to Karnataka's broader workforce transformation agenda. articles.title: Kyptec Automation Expands USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable Portfolio for High Speed Industrial Imaging and Machine Vision Systems
articles.summary: VMPL New Delhi [India], October 7: Kyptec Automation is strengthening its industrial imaging connectivity portfolio with the USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable developed for reliable communication between compatible industrial cameras and host computing systems used in machine vision, automated inspection and factory automation. The Kyptec Automation Machine Vision USB 3.0 A Male to Micro USB 3.0 Male With Screw Camera Cable combines a USB Type A connection for the host system with a Micro USB 3.0 connection incorporating locking screws for the camera side. The cable is available in standard lengths of 2 Meter, 3 Meter and 5 Meter, giving OEMs, machine builders and system integrators multiple options for different camera positions, industrial computer locations and machine geometries while remaining within one defined USB 3.0 machine vision connectivity platform. Modern machine vision systems depend on a complete imaging architecture in which the camera, lens, illumination, acquisition interface, cable, host controller, processing hardware and machine vision software must operate together. As industrial cameras capture increasingly detailed image information at higher acquisition rates, reliable communication between the camera and processing system becomes an important part of overall inspection stability. The USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable is therefore not simply a connection between two devices. It forms part of the image acquisition path through which industrial camera data must be transferred consistently to the host system for processing, measurement, identification and automated inspection. USB 3.0 connectivity is particularly relevant for compatible industrial imaging systems where high speed camera data needs to be transferred to an industrial computer or processing platform within the designed machine architecture. Selecting a USB 3.0 camera cable should therefore begin with the actual imaging requirement rather than connector compatibility alone. Camera resolution, frame rate, pixel format, acquisition frequency, cable length, host controller architecture, connector retention, routing conditions, machine movement and production duty cycle should all be considered before the final cable configuration is approved. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable uses a USB Type A male connector on the host side and a Micro USB 3.0 male connector with locking screws on the camera side. This camera side locking arrangement is particularly relevant to industrial imaging installations where the connection may need to remain secure throughout prolonged production operation. Industrial cameras can be installed inside inspection machines, beside conveyors, within automated assembly systems, above production lines or inside purpose built imaging stations. In these applications, cable security and controlled routing can become important elements of reliable camera integration. An industrial camera cable should also be evaluated according to its operating environment. Machine vision equipment can expose cable assemblies to repeated handling, movement, equipment vibration, constrained routing paths and continuous production operation. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable uses highly flexible PVC cable construction intended for industrial imaging applications. The cable architecture is designed for applications including machine vision systems, industrial cameras, scientific imaging, automated inspection, product testing, image recognition, data acquisition and factory automation. The relationship between camera bandwidth and cable architecture is another important consideration. A machine vision camera generates image data according to sensor resolution, frame rate, pixel format and acquisition settings. Increasing any of these parameters can increase the volume of data that must move through the complete imaging system. Engineers should therefore evaluate the USB 3.0 machine vision cable together with the camera and host architecture instead of assuming that interface designation alone guarantees the required system performance. The host controller, processing platform, acquisition software and storage architecture can all influence how successfully the complete system manages the required image stream. This becomes even more important where several industrial cameras are integrated into one inspection machine. Multiple cameras can create a significantly different system load compared with a single camera architecture. Engineers may need to consider how camera traffic is distributed across host controller resources, how images are processed, whether acquisition occurs simultaneously and what operating margin is required for continuous production. The cable remains one component within this complete data path, which is why machine vision connectivity should be qualified under the actual camera and host configuration that will be used in the production machine. Industrial camera connectivity should be engineered as part of the complete machine vision system rather than treated as an ordinary computer accessory, said Nitin Aggarwal, Co Founder and CEO of Kyptec Automation. When OEMs and system integrators design a USB 3.0 camera architecture, they need to consider camera data requirements, cable length, locking mechanism, routing, host controller capability and production conditions together. Our objective is to provide a structured USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable platform that supports reliable industrial camera integration across machine vision, automated inspection and factory automation systems. Connector retention is particularly important in industrial machinery because camera communication needs to remain stable during normal equipment operation. A locking USB 3.0 camera cable can provide additional mechanical retention at the industrial camera connection compared with a connector that relies only on insertion force. The locking screws incorporated into the Micro USB 3.0 camera side connection are intended to support secure installation with compatible industrial cameras. Correct installation should nevertheless include appropriate cable routing, strain management, connector clearance and suitable bend conditions so that mechanical forces are not unnecessarily transferred to the camera connector. Cable length should also be selected according to system geometry rather than simply choosing the longest available option. The Kyptec Automation USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable is available in standard 2 Meter, 3 Meter and 5 Meter lengths. Machine builders should evaluate the actual distance between camera and host system, cable tray routing, cabinet position, service accessibility and any movement within the machine before standardizing the required cable length. A correctly planned installation can reduce unnecessary cable loops, excessive tension and difficult routing while making machine commissioning and future maintenance more structured. The selection of a USB camera cable for machine vision also depends on how the camera is physically integrated into the equipment. A camera mounted close to an industrial computer can have very different routing requirements from a camera positioned remotely inside a large inspection machine. Similarly, a fixed camera installation can create different mechanical requirements from an application where part of the cable route is exposed to repeated movement. Defining these conditions early in the machine design process allows the connectivity architecture to be treated as an engineered subsystem rather than as a component selected after the camera installation has already been completed. For OEMs manufacturing multiple machines, standardization of the USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable can support repeatable engineering and production. Once camera type, host architecture, cable length and installation method have been qualified, manufacturers can define approved configurations for individual machine platforms. These configurations can become part of engineering drawings, bills of material, assembly documentation, commissioning procedures and replacement planning. A structured approach can also help system integrators maintain greater consistency when the same imaging architecture is deployed across multiple production lines or customer installations. Automated visual inspection is one of the environments where reliable camera connectivity becomes particularly important. Machine vision cameras may be used to inspect product dimensions, surface condition, component presence, assembly position, labels, printed information, packaging quality or other manufacturing characteristics. Images captured by the camera must reach the processing system so that software can analyse the inspection area and provide the required output within the machine cycle. Stable connectivity therefore contributes to the continuity of the complete acquisition and processing architecture. Industrial imaging installations also need to consider electrical and mechanical conditions surrounding the cable route. Industrial computers, motors, automation equipment, power cables, moving assemblies and control systems can all exist within the same machine environment. Engineers should plan the camera cable path carefully and maintain appropriate separation, routing discipline and mechanical protection according to the design of the equipment. Cable qualification should be performed with the actual industrial camera, host computer, acquisition settings and machine operating conditions rather than relying only on individual component specifications. The machine vision camera cable therefore needs to be understood as part of the wider industrial imaging system. Camera connectivity influences how the imaging hardware is installed, how reliably the camera communicates with the host and how easily the machine can be manufactured, commissioned and serviced. By developing a dedicated USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable platform, Kyptec Automation is focusing specifically on connectivity requirements associated with industrial cameras, machine vision systems and automated inspection rather than positioning the product as general purpose USB connectivity. The USB 3.0 machine vision cable category also supports the broader requirement for clearly defined machine vision components within OEM equipment. Engineering teams increasingly standardize cameras, optics, lighting, cables, computers and other components so that each machine configuration can be reproduced consistently. A defined industrial camera cable architecture allows cable length, connection type, locking method and routing requirement to become part of this standardization process. This can be particularly valuable in machines intended for continuous production where component consistency and serviceability are important considerations throughout the operational life of the equipment. Machine vision adoption continues to expand across electronics production, packaging, pharmaceutical inspection, automotive manufacturing, component measurement, product identification, assembly verification, surface inspection and many other factory automation environments. Although these applications can require different cameras, lenses, lighting arrangements and image processing methods, all of them depend on a reliable connection between the camera and processing system. USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable selection therefore represents an important engineering decision for applications using compatible USB industrial cameras. Kyptec Automation is strengthening its specialist machine vision connectivity portfolio around this system level requirement. The combination of USB 3.0 connectivity, USB Type A host interface, Micro USB 3.0 camera connection with locking screws, flexible cable construction and multiple standard length options provides OEMs and system integrators with a defined platform for compatible industrial imaging systems. The objective is to support camera connectivity across automated inspection, machine vision, scientific imaging, product testing, image recognition and factory automation applications while maintaining a clear relationship between camera requirements, cable architecture and host system design. By expanding its focus on USB 3.0 Machine Vision Camera Cable technology, Kyptec Automation is strengthening its position within industrial camera connectivity and machine vision system integration. The product platform addresses the practical relationship between high speed image acquisition, camera connection security, cable length planning, host architecture, machine layout and long term industrial operation. For OEMs, machine builders and system integrators developing modern automated inspection equipment, this complete system perspective provides a structured foundation for selecting and standardizing camera connectivity within machine vision applications.
